name: Barbell Back Squat
instructions: Set the barbell in a rack at upper-chest height, step under it, and rest it across your upper traps with hands gripped firmly just outside shoulder width.
Unrack by extending your knees and hips together, take two or three short steps back, and set your feet shoulder-width apart with toes turned out slightly.
Brace your core, keep your chest up, and descend by bending your hips and knees together until your thighs reach at least parallel to the floor.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes and your whole foot flat on the floor throughout the descent.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up, extending your knees and hips until fully upright.
Re-brace and repeat for the prescribed reps, then walk the bar back into the rack to finish.
formCues: Brace your core before every descent
Knees track over toes
Drive through mid-foot and heel
Keep chest tall and back neutral
commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave inward
Rounding the lower back at the bottom
Rising onto the toes and lifting the heels

name: Barbell Front Squat
instructions: Set the bar in a rack at upper-chest height and rest it across the front of your shoulders, on top of your front delts.
Secure the bar with a clean grip (fingers under the bar) or a crossed-arm grip, keeping your elbows pointed high and forward.
Unrack the bar, step back, and set your feet shoulder-width apart with toes turned out slightly.
Brace your core and descend by bending your knees and hips, keeping your torso as upright as possible until your thighs reach parallel.
Drive through your whole foot to stand tall, keeping your elbows high so the bar stays supported on your shoulders.
Re-brace and repeat for the prescribed reps, then return the bar to the rack to finish.
formCues: Keep elbows high to support the bar
Stay upright through the torso
Brace hard to protect the spine
Knees track over toes
commonMistakes: Dropping the elbows so the bar rolls forward
Letting the torso pitch forward and the upper back round
Rising onto the toes and lifting the heels

name: Goblet Squat
instructions: Hold one dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against your chest, cupping the top head with both hands just under your chin.
Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width and your toes turned out slightly.
Brace your core, keep your chest up, and point your elbows down.
Sit your hips back and down, bending your knees until your elbows reach the inside of your knees or your thighs are parallel.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up to full height, keeping the weight tight against your chest.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.
formCues: Hold the weight tight to your chest
Keep elbows pointing down
Sit between your hips, chest tall
Push knees out over toes
commonMistakes: Letting the chest collapse forward
Heels rising off the floor
Knees caving inward

name: Leg Press
instructions: Sit in the leg press machine with your back and head flat against the pad and place your feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform.
Release the safety handles and extend your legs to take the weight, keeping a slight bend in your knees rather than locking out hard.
Lower the platform by bending your knees toward your chest until they reach roughly 90 degrees, or until your lower back starts to lift off the pad.
Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and your hips planted on the seat throughout.
Press through your whole foot to extend your legs back to the start without slamming into a hard lockout.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, then re-engage the safety handles to finish.
formCues: Keep your lower back flat on the pad
Don't lock the knees aggressively
Knees track in line with toes
Push through the whole foot
commonMistakes: Lowering so deep the hips and lower back round off the pad
Locking out the knees forcefully
Letting the knees cave inward

name: Leg Extension
instructions: Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot point.
Position the shin pad just above your ankles and grip the handles at your sides.
Brace and extend your knees to lift the pad, straightening your legs under control.
Pause briefly at the top with your quads fully contracted, without snapping into a hard lockout.
Lower the weight slowly under control until your knees return to about 90 degrees.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.
formCues: Align knees with the machine pivot
Control the lowering phase
Squeeze the quads at the top
Keep hips planted on the seat
commonMistakes: Using momentum to swing the weight up
Snapping into a violent lockout
Letting the weight drop quickly on the way down

name: Walking Lunge
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, feet hip-width apart and core braced.
Take a controlled step forward with one leg, landing on your whole foot.
Lower your body by bending both knees until your back knee nearly touches the floor and your front thigh is about parallel.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee tracking over your toes rather than collapsing inward.
Drive through your front foot to bring your back leg forward into the next step, alternating legs as you walk.
Continue for the prescribed reps per leg, keeping each step controlled.
formCues: Keep your torso tall and core braced
Front knee tracks over the toes
Lower the back knee under control
Drive through the front foot to stand
commonMistakes: Letting the front knee cave inward
Leaning the torso too far forward
Taking too short a step so the knee shoots past the toes

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Stand a couple of feet in front of a bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Place the top of one foot behind you on the bench, with your front foot planted far enough forward that your shin stays near vertical at the bottom.
Brace your core and keep your torso tall with a slight forward lean.
Lower yourself by bending your front knee until your front thigh reaches about parallel and your back knee drops toward the floor.
Drive through your front foot to return to the start, keeping the front knee tracking over your toes.
Complete all reps on one leg, then switch sides.
formCues: Keep the front shin near vertical
Keep most of the weight on the front foot
Brace your core and stay tall
Control the descent
commonMistakes: Placing the front foot too close so the knee drifts far past the toes
Pushing off the back foot instead of loading the front leg
Letting the front knee collapse inward

name: Step-Up
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy box or bench of about knee height, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Place one whole foot flat on top of the box with your shin roughly vertical.
Brace your core and drive through the heel of the top foot to stand fully upright on the box, bringing the trailing foot up.
Let the top leg do the work; avoid pushing off the floor with the bottom foot.
Step back down under control with the same lead leg, returning to the floor softly.
Complete the prescribed reps, then switch your lead leg.
formCues: Drive through the heel of the top foot
Keep your torso tall and core braced
Control the step down
Place the full foot on the box
commonMistakes: Pushing off the bottom foot for momentum
Using a box so high the knee passes well past the toes
Dropping down uncontrolled instead of lowering
